  comment = "#>"

The `equationer` package provides an extensible, R6-registry based framework for extracting clean, plain-text regression formulas, group-level random effect equations, and subgroup factor projections from linear, generalized linear, and mixed-effects models.

```{r setup}
library(equationer)
```

## 1. Basic Usage with Standard Linear Models (`lm`)

Extracting plain-text formulas from standard `lm` objects is simple.

```{r lm-example}
# Fit a multiple linear regression model
fit_lm <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)

# Extract global equation
eq_lm <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_lm, digits = 3)
print(eq_lm)
```

You can convert the resulting `equation_collection` into a standard `data.frame` for downstream processing, report exports, or table output:

```{r lm-dataframe}
as.data.frame(eq_lm)
```

---

## 2. Subgroup Equation Extraction (`by_factor`)

When models contain categorical factors or factor interactions, `equationer` can project subgroup-specific regression equations across the unique levels of factor variables using its vectorized model-matrix projection engine.

```{r subgroup-example}
# Prepare data with categorical factor
model_data <- transform(mtcars, cyl = factor(cyl))

# Fit a model with continuous and factor terms
fit_factor <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = model_data)

# Extract subgroup equations stratified by the factor 'cyl'
eq_subgroups <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_factor, by_factor = "cyl", digits = 2)
print(eq_subgroups)
```

---

## 3a. Mixed-Effects Models (`lme4`) & Group-Level Random Equations

`equationer` seamlessly processes linear mixed-effects models fitted with `lme4::lmer`. You can extract both the population-level (fixed-effects) equation or individual subject/group-specific equations that incorporate estimated random intercepts and slopes.

### Population-Level (Fixed Effects) Equation

```{r lmer-global}
library(lme4)

# Fit a linear mixed-effects model on sleepstudy dataset
fit_lmer <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)

# Extract overall population fixed-effects equation
eq_lmer_fixed <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_lmer, digits = 2)
print(eq_lmer_fixed)
```

### Subject/Group-Level Random Effect Equations

When analyzing hierarchical data, you often need individual equations for each group or subject that combine fixed effects with conditional modes (random effects):

```{r lmer-subject-level}
# Extract subject-specific equations for all subjects in the random effect grouping
eq_lmer_subjects <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_lmer, digits = 2, by_subject = TRUE)
print(eq_lmer_subjects)
```

## 3b. Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Models with `glmmTMB`

`equationer` natively supports model objects fitted with `glmmTMB`.

```{r glmmtmb-example, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(glmmTMB)

# Fit a mixed-effects model using glmmTMB
fit_tmb <- glmmTMB(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)

# 1. Extract population-level global fixed-effects equation
eq_tmb_global <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_tmb, digits = 2)
print(eq_tmb_global)

# 2. Extract subject-specific equations incorporating random effects
eq_tmb_subjects <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_tmb, digits = 2, by_subject = TRUE)

# View first 5 subject-specific equations
head(as.data.frame(eq_tmb_subjects), 5)
```

---

## 4. Extending `equationer`: Writing Custom Adapters (`mgcv::gam`)

`equationer` uses an internal R6 class registry. If you work with a model framework that is not supported out of the box, you can define a custom `ModelAdapter` subclass and register it via `register_model_adapter()`.

Below is a complete, production-ready example demonstrating how to build an adapter for Generalized Additive Models fitted with `mgcv::gam`.

### Step 1: Define the R6 Adapter Class

```r
library(mgcv)

#' Custom Model Adapter for mgcv::gam Objects
AdapterGAM <- R6::R6Class("AdapterGAM",
  inherit = ModelAdapter,
  public = list(
    get_response_name = function() {
      # Extract response term name from model formula
      as.character(stats::formula(self$model))[2]
    },
    
    get_fixed_effects = function() {
      # Extract parametric fixed-effect coefficients
      coef(self$model)
    },
    
    get_data = function() {
      # Extract model frame used during fitting
      self$model$model
    },
    
    get_error_label = function() {
      # Define appropriate error suffix representation
      " + \u03B5"
    }
  )
)
```

### Step 2: Register the Adapter Class

Register your custom class generator with the package registry:

```r
# Register AdapterGAM for model objects of class "gam"
register_model_adapter("gam", AdapterGAM)
```

### Step 3: Extract Equations from a `gam` Model

Once registered, any fitted `gam` model can be passed directly to `extract_mixed_equation()`:

```r
# Fit a GAM with parametric terms
fit_gam <- gam(mpg ~ wt + hp + gear, data = mtcars)

# Extract equation using the registered custom adapter
eq_gam <- extract_mixed_equation(fit_gam, digits = 2)
print(eq_gam)
```
